newsitem.title: USA: Plaintiffs ask for damages to punish Reynolds.
newsitem.headline: Plaintiffs ask for damages to punish Reynolds.

text.p: Plaintiffs attorney Ron Motley said in closing arguments that RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co should be punished to end a company strategy of creating doubt that cigarettes cause illness, but he named no figure for those damages.

Motley told the six-member jury hearing a wrongful death lawsuit against Reynolds that the company bore responsibility for smoker Jean Connor's death and for refusing to admit that cigarettes could be harmful to health.
"You've got to stop that. Please stop that," Motley said.
Connor, a heavy smoker from the time she was a teen-ager, died of lung cancer in 1995. Her sister, Dana Raulerson, sued the tobacco company on behalf of her children and her estate.

Motley said valued the loss to Connor's estate at $250,000-$300,000, saying she could have lived another 31 years. He also said her children must be compensated for the two years they saw their mother suffer after she was diagnosed with lung cancer, and for 31 years that they would not have her in their lives. He said punitive damaages should be well in excess of those losses but gave no figure for punitive damages.
Motley will have another chance to address the jury before it begins deliberations.
"I think the evidence in this case justifies an award, well, multiplies in excess of whatever you award in actual damages," Motley said.
"Would a million dollars punish them? Will it stop them? What's going to stop them?" he asked.
